title: Find The True Profit Behind Your ROAS.
subtitle: A 4x ROAS can still lose money once product, shipping and fees come out. 21 questions score your profit engine and give you the break-even ROAS you need before scaling pays. Takes 8 minutes.

low.headline: You are scaling on a number that hides your losses
low.text: Revenue and ROAS both look fine while the order underneath them loses money. Until you know your real contribution margin after product, shipping and fees, every spend increase is a bet you cannot price. This is the first thing to fix because every other decision downstream inherits the blind spot.
steps: Calculate contribution margin on your top 5 products this week: price minus landed cost, shipping, fees and a return allowance
Find the two products where a good ROAS still loses money and pause spend on them
Set one number, contribution margin per order, that every campaign decision has to clear

mid.headline: You know your margin, but only when you sit down to find it
mid.text: You can produce a real margin number, but it lives in a spreadsheet you rebuild by hand, so it is always a week behind the decisions it should be driving. The move is making that number live and per order so it shows up before you scale, not after.
steps: Pull margin by SKU into one view and sort it worst to best
Wire landed cost, shipping and fees into that view so it updates without a manual rebuild
Review your bottom five margin products monthly and decide keep, reprice or cut

high.headline: Your margin is visible, now make it a weapon
high.text: You see true margin per order and per product, which most brands your size never do. The next layer is using it to steer spend automatically toward the products and cohorts that actually compound profit.
steps: Route ad budget by product-level contribution, not blended ROAS
Flag any SKU whose margin drops below target and pull it from active campaigns automatically
Feed margin by cohort into your retention and bundling decisions

low.headline: A 4x ROAS can still be a loss, and right now you would not catch it
low.text: Optimizing to ROAS alone means the platform decides what winning looks like, and the platform does not know your costs. On a $60 order with $50 of product, shipping and fees, a 4x ROAS loses money on every sale. Without a break-even ROAS tied to your real costs, you are scaling whatever Meta says is good.
steps: Calculate your break-even ROAS from real costs: order value divided by contribution margin per order
Put that break-even line on the same screen as your campaign ROAS so the gap is obvious
Reconcile one week of platform-reported revenue against actual orders in the bank

mid.headline: You watch profit sometimes, ROAS always
mid.text: You know ROAS can lie, and you glance at profit, but the day-to-day steering still runs on the platform number. Closing that gap means profit per order becomes the metric campaigns are judged on, checked as often as ROAS is.
steps: Set a break-even ROAS per product and update it when costs move
Move to channel-level profit, reconciled weekly against the bank
Kill any campaign that sits below break-even for three days, regardless of reported ROAS

high.headline: You steer on profit, now automate the guardrails
high.text: Profit per order runs your decisions and you already discount platform numbers. The next step is turning your break-even discipline into automated rules so nothing scales past the point where it stops making money.
steps: Trigger alerts the moment a campaign crosses below its product break-even ROAS
Blend true contribution across channels so overlapping attribution stops inflating winners
Tie budget shifts to marginal profit, not last-click ROAS

low.headline: Half your costs are missing from the number you call profit
low.text: When COGS is stale and shipping, fees and overhead are left out, the profit figure you trust is fiction. It is almost always more optimistic than reality, which is why brands feel busy and broke at the same time. Getting every real cost into one per-order figure is the foundation everything else sits on.
steps: Rebuild landed cost for your top products including freight, duties and packaging
Pull last month's real shipping and processing fees and divide by orders to get a true per-order rate
Add a loaded overhead rate so software and team cost stop hiding

mid.headline: Your costs are mostly there, but manual and lagging
mid.text: You capture most real costs, yet the pieces live in different places and get updated on memory. That lag is where margin quietly drifts. Automating the cost inputs keeps your profit number honest without a monthly reconstruction.
steps: Connect COGS and 3PL costs so they update without a manual edit
Pull processor fees per transaction instead of a flat percentage
Set a monthly check to confirm allocated overhead still matches the real stack

high.headline: Your cost accounting is tight, keep it self-correcting
high.text: Real landed cost, fulfillment, fees and overhead all reach your per-order margin, which is rare. The job now is keeping it accurate automatically as suppliers, carriers and your tool stack change under you.
steps: Alert on any landed-cost change that moves a product below its margin target
Reconcile fees and shipping against statements automatically each month
Re-allocate overhead on a schedule as headcount and software shift

low.headline: You are scaling on the gas pedal and reading the mirror late
low.text: When the decision to scale runs on weekly ROAS and losers get caught days after they start bleeding, growth costs you more than it returns. Scaling discipline means the signal to add or cut spend is profit, and it reaches you fast enough to act on the same day.
steps: Define the contribution number a campaign must hold before it earns more budget
Set a same-day rule to pause anything that drops below break-even
Model the cash tied up before your next spend increase, not after

Run a margin-tied price or bundle test every month to protect AOV as spend grows
